**About VetPowered LLC**
========================


VetPowered was founded in 2009 to support Workshops for Warriors (wfw.org), an accredited 501(c)(3\) nonprofit school that trains, certifies, and places veterans and transitioning service members into dignified lifelong careers in advanced manufacturing to Rebuild America’s Manufacturing Force…One Veteran at a Time. Workshops for Warriors has trained and certified 1,776 veterans and transitioning service members, awarded nearly 23,000 industry credentials, and placed graduates at 522 companies across 49 states. The average starting wage for a WFW graduate is $63,500\.


Our goal is to train veterans for dignified lifelong careers and make America the world’s manufacturing superpower again.


That is the story almost nobody has heard. This role exists to change that, and to turn the telling of it into purchase orders, partnerships, and product revenue. This will allow us to create scholarships, provide housing, and build brighter futures for the men and women who honorably served our nation.

**Position Overview**
=====================


VetPowered, LLC is seeking a dynamic and highly organized candidate for the position of Personal Aide to the Chief Executive Officer. In this vital role, you will serve as primary support for a busy CEO, helping ensure smooth daily operations and efficient management of personal and administrative tasks.


The CEO has many time\-sensitive commitments, both professionally and personally, and is continually creating and pursuing growth opportunities for multi\-million\-dollar organizations. Your proactive approach, exceptional organizational skills, and attention to detail will help create an efficient and productive working environment.


Most importantly, this position requires patience, a pleasant demeanor, the ability to listen well, a sense of urgency, and the ability to follow directions. Reliability is a must.


This is a full personal and administrative support position and is not appropriate for candidates who wish to perform only in\-office administrative duties. Candidates with prior experience assisting very busy, Type A individuals are encouraged to apply. The information below is intended to provide transparent expectations for this key support role.

**Purpose of the Position**
===========================


At VetPowered, LLC, the Personal Aide exists so that the Chief Executive Officer can spend his time on the work that only he can do. The role removes recurring, time\-consuming, and personal tasks that would otherwise consume hours of every day or be improperly assigned to senior officers of the organization.


This position performs work that would not be asked of the Chief Operating Officer, Chief of Staff, or Executive Aide. That distinction defines the role.


The Personal Aide is accountable for the readiness and order of the Chief Executive Officer’s working environment, the continuity of his personal and household affairs, and the complete execution of any assigned task that is legal, ethical, safe, and consistent with the mission.


This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working behind the scenes to keep things organized. The ideal candidate will anticipate the CEO’s needs, maintain workspace readiness, and take pride in making his day easier. This hands\-on role requires discretion, flexibility, and the ability to thrive in a fast\-paced environment where no two days are the same.

**Duties, Responsibilities \& Expectations**
============================================

**Workspace Readiness**
-----------------------


The office of the Chief Executive Officer and all adjoining workspaces are the responsibility of this position.

* Ensure the office, desk, work surfaces, and adjoining workspaces are clean, cleared, vacuumed, and organized before the Chief Executive Officer arrives each morning.
* Maintain order in the space throughout the day and reset it at the close of business.
* No outside cleaning contractor, building custodial staff, or other personnel may clean or organize the personal space of the Chief Executive Officer. This work is performed by the Personal Aide.
* Maintain supplies, materials, and equipment so that nothing is missing when it is needed.

**Meal Service and Hospitality**
--------------------------------


Meals with senior staff and guests are a working instrument of leadership. This position ensures those meals happen properly without consuming the time of the Chief Executive Officer or other officers of the organization.

* Order, obtain, prepare, plate, and serve breakfast, lunch, dinner, refreshments, and snacks for the Chief Executive Officer and for guests or staff members he designates.
* Set the table and surrounding space in advance so that the Chief Executive Officer and his guests sit down to a complete and ready setting.
* Ensure meals are fresh, wholesome, and nutritious, while accounting for the dietary requirements of guests.
* Clear, clean, and reset the space at the conclusion of the meal without interrupting work in progress.
* Provide hospitality support for visitors, tours, and guests hosted by the Chief Executive Officer.

**Errands, Vehicles, and Personal Logistics**
---------------------------------------------

* Execute personal and business errands, including dry cleaning, laundry, shoe repair, shopping, purchasing, post office visits, pickups, deliveries, and returns.
* Provide basic dog care and complete other personal errands as directed.
* Travel to the residence and vehicles of the Chief Executive Officer to retrieve, deliver, or place items as directed.
* Manage personal vehicle administration, including registration, insurance documentation, service scheduling, and ensuring current documents are maintained in each vehicle.

Overview:
**LEARN Behavioral** is a national organization made up of dedicated and caring individuals with the sole purpose of nurturing children with autism and special needs to lead resilient and fulfilling lives. We specialize in contemporary, evidence based applied behavior analysis to deliver personalized treatment plans, backed by 20 years of clinical insights. We are proud to be a part of each family’s journey and share in the experience of finding success for every child, and family, in our care. If you share a similar passion for nurturing and empowering the success of others, along with the opportunity to have an impact on the lives of others, we are eager to connect with you!  

LEARN Behavioral hiring an **Executive Director of Advocacy**!  

Every day, families across the country are waiting — for a payor approval, for a regulatory fix, for someone in the room who understands both the policy and the child behind it. At LEARN Behavioral, we believe every autistic individual deserves access to the care that helps them thrive, and we're looking for an individual to lead our Advocacy efforts and help make that a reality in every community we serve.  

This is a rare opportunity to sit at the intersection of mission and policy — shaping the legislative and regulatory landscape for autism services while serving as a trusted voice for one of the country's leading providers of ABA and autism care.
Who We’re Looking For:

We are seeking an individual who is excited to develop and execute plans that drive meaningful, lasting impact across the organization and the field.  

As the leader of LEARN’s advocacy efforts, you will lead the company efforts to improve access to care for autistic individuals — especially clients covered by Medicaid — in partnership with executive management, local leadership, and third\-party lobbyists. You'll work hand\-in\-hand with regional leaders to advance legislative and regulatory reforms that support our mission and business goals, and you'll serve as LEARN's primary point of contact with national and regional industry associations.
What You Have:
* Bachelor's degree and a minimum of 10 years of relevant experience in advocacy, government relations, public policy, or a closely related field. Preference for individuals with direct experience in the field of ABA.
* Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate complex policy issues into actionable advocacy strategies.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage and collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders — from clinicians to legislators to payors.
* A track record of working independently and as part of a team in a fast\-paced, dynamic environment.
* Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines at once.
* Willingness to travel to represent LEARN in key markets and forums.


What You’ll Be Doing:
* Develop and implement advocacy initiatives in key markets alongside internal stakeholders, with a particular focus on Medicaid programs.
* Partner with local leadership to weave advocacy priorities into broader business strategy and objectives.
* Track and report on legislation and regulations that could affect access to care, keeping the organization ahead of change rather than reacting to it.
* Build and sustain relationships with key external stakeholders — legislators, regulators, payors, and industry partners.
* Represent LEARN at relevant forums, conferences, and events, serving as a visible and credible voice for the field.
* Keep executive management informed on developments that could impact the organization.
* Partner with Payor relations and RCM team on reimbursement related issues
* Liaise with key industry groups

Achievement First (AF) is a nonprofit 501(c)(3\) organization supporting 39 public charter schools across New York, Connecticut, and Rhode Island. For more than 25 years, AF has been recognized as one of the top tuition\-free public charter school networks in the country. We are committed to creating schools of academic excellence within nurturing environments — schools that prepare students to be college\-ready and to pursue and succeed in whatever paths they choose in life.



The majority of AF students are Black and Latinx children from low\-income families, many of whom will be the first in their families to graduate from college. The LEAH (Leaders through Education, Action, and Hope) Project seeks a visionary, entrepreneurial, and relationship\-driven leader to serve as its next Executive Director. At a pivotal moment in the program's evolution, the Executive Director will be responsible for leading LEAH into its next chapter of growth, sustainability, and impact.


Founded in memory of Leah Deni, a youth worker with a passion for science, the LEAH Project promotes the power of youth—especially Black, Indigenous, People of Color (BIPOC), first\-generation, and historically underrepresented youth—to diversify science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields. The Executive Director will inherit a highly respected program with a strong and experienced team, longstanding partnerships across Boston's STEM ecosystem, a dedicated Advisory Board, and a solid foundation for future growth. **REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS FOR INTERIM EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR \& EXECUTIVE SEARCH LEADERSHIP**



 Avenues for Youth is seeking a candidate for a contract position of Interim Executive Director. This is an opportunity to lead a growing youth\-centered organization partnering with young people experiencing homelessness and to facilitate an inclusive and values\-focused search for a new permanent Executive Director.


**ABOUT AVENUES FOR YOUTH**



For 30 years, Avenues has supported youth ages 16\-24 in Hennepin County. Whether a young person needs a place to stay for just one night, or a year and a half, Avenues partners with youth to find their path out of homelessness. We do that by providing a stable home, building trusting relationships, and supporting the youth’s education, career, health and wellness and housing goals. Avenues operates two shelter/transitional living programs for young people, one in North Minneapolis and one in Brooklyn Park, temporary supportive housing for young families, outreach and drop\-in services, and affordable housing for young people exiting homelessness. Avenues also operates two community\-based programs, our ConneQT Host Home Program and our scattered site, apartment\-based Avenues for Youth Families program. 2026 has been a year of significant growth for our organization – we closed on a capacity campaign, built a new building in North Minneapolis, and expanded programming.


**OUR MISSION**



Avenues partners with youth experiencing homelessness to achieve their dreams.



**OUR VISION**



A community where all youth flourish.


**OUR VALUES**



Avenues work is guided by the 9 Evidence\-based, Guiding Principles to Help Youth Overcome Homelessness and our core values: Equity, Community, Respect \+ Dignity, Trust, Liberation, and Anti\-oppression.



At Avenues, we believe:


* Homelessness does not define a person. It is just one part of a journey that we are here to help young people navigate.


* Nearly all youth experiencing homelessness have or are experiencing trauma. Therefore, mental health is at the center of all our work.


* There is no one reason why youth experience homelessness – it’s intersectional. Systems of oppression, racism and poverty are some of the root causes of homelessness. Without addressing these systems, homelessness will persist.


* Youth are resilient, inspiring, and the drivers of their own journey. With stability, trust and youth\-centered supports, their dreams can become reality.


**KEY ROLES**



With support from the Associate Executive Director, Director of Advancement, and the Director of Finance, the selected applicant will provide administrative, financial, personnel, and program management for the organization. They will oversee the day\-to\-day operations of the work, guide a diverse and talented staff, ensure the financial stability of the organization in a time of growth, and represent Avenues within the community and, to a more limited extent, with funders. They will also work with the Board of Directors to conduct a search for a permanent director. Avenues is a values\-guided organization – the 9 Guiding Principles and the 6 organizational values are key to who we are and how we do our work. It’s important that the contracted Interim Executive Director understand and live in those values as they provide leadership for the organization and the search for the next permanent Executive Director.


**LEADERSHIP \& MANAGEMENT**


* Work with program team to ensure excellent inclusive programming continues to support young people in finding and maintaining housing and exiting into safe and stable housing


* Work with the Director of Finance to maintain the fiscal health of the organization and plan resources according to programming and administrative needs


* Support the Director of Advancement in raising funds from government, foundation, and individual donors and communicating the work of Avenues in the community


* Partner with the Associate Executive Director in managing the human resources, operation, and infrastructure of the organization


* Ensure proper oversight of the organization by providing consistent support and updates to the Board of Directors, working in partnership with the Board Officers and Committee Chairs


* Ensure compliance with all federal and state laws and execute legal documents on behalf of the Board of Directors


* Serve as representative for the organization with funders, community members, government funders, and media (lobbying is not required of this role) EXECUTIVE SEARCH


* Conduct interviews and focus groups to identify the key competencies and skillsets needed for the next permanent Executive Director



 • Develop the necessary infrastructure to ensure that young people, staff, and Board can participate in the search process • Create and execute a timeline to hire the permanent Executive Director by mid\-2027


**THIS IS THE OPPORTUNITY FOR YOU IF…**


* You enjoy mission\-driven work and feel aligned with our youth\- and justice\-centered values.



 • You have experience leading programs or organizations through times of transition. • You like to collaborate closely with a team and foster an environment of transparency and cooperation.


* You manage well in unpredictable circumstances and step up when help is needed.


* You can manage competing priorities and deal with multiple important factors simultaneously.


* You are ready to lead a group of engaged young people, staff, and board members in an executive search.


**TERM**



This is a temporary, contract role, with an estimated 25\-30 hours/week, not benefits eligible. The contract will begin in December 2026 and end when the new permanent Executive Director begins in mid\-2027\. The applicant selected for this position is not eligible to apply for the permanent Executive Director role.

25 years in, Upwardly Global (UpGlo) has a proven program, a compelling case for support, and a major donor base that is far smaller than that case warrants. We are hiring a major gifts leader to change that, primarily by finding, qualifying, and closing donors who do not know us yet.

**Why This Role, Why Now**


Upwardly Global (UpGlo) is a national nonprofit that helps immigrants, refugees, and asylees rebuild their professional careers in the United States. We work at both the direct service and system\-change levels, building a more inclusive workforce and economy by ensuring everyone can fully use their skills and talents.

**Here is what that means for a fundraiser:**

* The case for support is concrete and measurable. We can show a donor the economic return on a placed professional, not just a sentiment. That is a rare advantage in a first major gift conversation.
* The prospect universe is genuinely underworked. Individual giving currently accounts for roughly $2M of our $14M in annual revenue. **EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**


The LEAH (Leaders through Education, Action, and Hope) Project seeks a visionary, entrepreneurial, and relationship\-driven leader to serve as its next Executive Director. At a pivotal moment in the program's evolution, the Executive Director will be responsible for leading LEAH into its next chapter of growth, sustainability, and impact.


Founded in memory of Leah Deni, a youth worker with a passion for science, the LEAH Project promotes the power of youth—especially Black, Indigenous, People of Color (BIPOC), first\-generation, and historically underrepresented youth—to diversify science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields. Through paid internships, college and career readiness programming, mentoring, and youth leadership opportunities, LEAH equips young people with the skills, confidence, networks, and experiences needed to thrive in STEM education and careers.


Over the past two decades, LEAH has served more than 1,000 high school students and 7,000 elementary school students across Greater Boston. Today, the program supports more than 150 high school and college\-aged youth annually and has achieved exceptional outcomes, including a 99% high school graduation rate and 95% college enrollment rate among participants.


The Executive Director will inherit a highly respected program with a strong and experienced team, longstanding partnerships across Boston's STEM ecosystem, a dedicated Advisory Board, and a solid foundation for future growth. Following a period of successful stabilization and strategic planning, LEAH is well\-positioned to expand its impact, diversify its revenue streams, and explore emerging opportunities in sectors such as climate resilience, clean energy and life sciences.


Reporting to HRiA’s Managing Director of Capacity Building Assistance, the Executive Director will lead and manage an annual operating budget of approximately $1\.2 million and drive efforts to diversify and grow LEAH’s revenue toward a sustainable future operating budget exceeding $2M\+.


The ideal candidate is a proven fundraiser and strategic leader who is energized by youth development, passionate about educational and economic opportunity, and excited to build the partnerships, visibility, and resources necessary to help LEAH thrive for the next generation of young people.


The LEAH Project seeks a leader who can inspire confidence, build meaningful relationships, secure resources, and champion opportunities for young people. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable meeting with a major donor, collaborating with a corporate partner, mentoring a staff member, engaging an Advisory Board member, or celebrating the accomplishments of a young person discovering their future.

 **ABOUT HEALTH RESOURCES IN ACTION**


The LEAH Project is a program of Health Resources in Action (HRiA), a national nonprofit organization working to improve and reimagine public health by transforming the policies, systems, and practices that improve health and advance equity.


Since joining HRiA in 2013, LEAH has benefited from the organization's strong infrastructure, financial stewardship, and commitment to creating opportunities for communities that have historically been excluded from educational and economic advancement.


As a program of HRiA, LEAH benefits from the infrastructure and shared services of a larger nonprofit organization, including finance, human resources, legal, IT, and other administrative functions. This structure allows the Executive Director to focus primarily on strategy, fundraising, organizational leadership, partnerships, and program oversight while working closely with HRiA colleagues who provide operational and administrative support.

 **THE OPPORTUNITY / OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES FOR THE POSITION TITLE**


The next Executive Director will have the opportunity to lead a highly respected program at a moment of possibility and growth.


Over the past year, LEAH has undergone a period of strategic stabilization and planning in response to shifts in the funding landscape. Building upon a strong foundation of programmatic excellence, exceptional youth outcomes, committed staff, and longstanding partnerships, LEAH is now poised to expand its reach and influence.


The Executive Director will build upon LEAH's strong foundation to lead the organization's next phase of growth, sustainability, and impact. This role requires a strategic and externally focused leader who can expand fundraising efforts, deepen partnerships, strengthen LEAH's visibility and influence, and ensure continued excellence in youth programming. Key responsibilities include:
